question: Which of the following stages of an automatic transmission system locks the transmission, restricting a vehicle from moving?
solution:
The correct answer is __Park (P) stage__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Park (P) stage__ is a gear position in automatic transmission systems.
 
• In the Park (P) stage, the transmission locks the vehicle's drivetrain, preventing any movement.
 
• This setting is primarily used when the vehicle is stationary.
 
• It ensures the safety of the vehicle by restricting unintentional rolling or movement.
 
• The Park stage engages a mechanism known as a parking pawl, which locks the transmission output shaft.
 
• Drivers are recommended to use this stage along with the parking brake for added safety.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Low (L) stage:**

 
 
• In this gear, the transmission limits the vehicle to lower speeds and provides higher torque.
 
• It is useful in situations like climbing steep hills or towing heavy loads.
 
 
 
• **Drive (D) stage:**
 
 
• The Drive stage allows the vehicle to move forward and automatically selects gears based on speed and load.
 
• It is commonly used for regular driving.
 
 
 
• **Neutral (N) stage:**
 
 
• In Neutral, the transmission disconnects the engine from the drivetrain.
 
• The vehicle can roll freely if not secured with brakes.
